description: Baseline on main after user committed workspace. Current Telegram parity penalty is 125: dock and preview headers still include extra leading icons, manager header still uses kind icon instead of expand chevron, and browser sheet entry motion still uses modal-feeling scale/alpha constants.

asi.hypothesis: Measure current main-branch implementation before making Telegram-alignment changes to dock chrome and browser-sheet motion.
asi.rollback_reason: Baseline is not an improvement; recording only to establish the starting metric for subsequent experiments.
asi.next_action_hint: First real experiment should remove extra leading icons from dock/transition/manager headers, switch manager right icon to expand chevron, and update tests/benchmark accordingly.

description: Experiment 1: aligned dock and preview headers to Telegram’s minimal tab chrome and softened browser sheet entry motion. Removed extra leading icon from collapsed dock, transition dock surface, and manager preview header; changed manager right-side affordance to expand chevron; reduced modal scale/alpha and scrim intensity in AppBrowserSheetContainer. Benchmark penalty dropped from 125 to 0 and targeted checks passed.

asi.hypothesis: Telegram parity will improve sharply if dock/manager headers are reduced to left close + centered title + right expand, and if browser sheet entry motion is made less modal.
asi.learned: The benchmark’s biggest parity gaps were concentrated in redundant preview header iconography and overly modal sheet constants. These were easy wins and passed correctness checks cleanly.
asi.next_action_hint: Next iteration should target dynamic smoothness beyond static chrome parity: manager open/close easing, dock-to-manager continuity, and the abrupt browser full-screen presentation feel that still likely needs better geometry/motion orchestration.

name: Telegram browser tabs manager motion smoothness

description: Baseline for motion-smoothness round. Current motion penalty is 85 because dismissBrowserTabsManager still does not enqueue CloseManager, manager close timing is shorter than Telegram overlay timing, and manager presentation still starts too low and too faded.

asi.hypothesis: Measure remaining dynamic smoothness gaps after the prior chrome-parity keep.
asi.rollback_reason: Baseline is only for reference and does not improve the new primary metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Add explicit CloseManager transition wiring on dismiss, lengthen manager close timing to match Telegram-style overlay cadence, and reduce manager initial translation/fade heaviness.

description: Experiment 2: improved tabs-manager motion continuity. Added explicit CloseManager transition wiring when dismissing multi-tab manager, increased manager close timing to 320ms to match Telegram overlay cadence, and tuned manager presentation to start closer to dock with higher initial alpha. Motion penalty dropped from 85 to 0 and targeted checks passed.

asi.hypothesis: Telegram-style smoothness improves if manager dismiss explicitly transitions back toward dock, manager close timing matches open timing, and manager content enters with less lift/fade.
asi.learned: The remaining tracked motion gaps were all shell-level orchestration/tuning issues rather than feature runtime logic. Pure helper extraction made them easy to verify with unit tests.
asi.next_action_hint: Next experiment should target the remaining real-world feel gap not covered by current static metrics: browser sheet open/dock restore continuity, especially the abrupt full-screen jump when a browser comes foreground.

description: Baseline for browser restore continuity. Current penalty is 80 because dock-restored browser entries are not explicitly marked as restored-from-dock, AppRoot does not propagate that semantic into AppBrowserSheetContainer, and the sheet container still handles restored foreground activation like a fresh open.

asi.hypothesis: Measure restore-specific continuity gaps after shell motion improvements.
asi.rollback_reason: Baseline only establishes the new metric and does not improve it.
asi.next_action_hint: Add restoredFromDock marker to BrowserHostBrowserEntry, set it during restoreDockedSession for browser entries, propagate it from AppRoot into AppBrowserSheetContainer, and give the sheet container a non-fresh-open restored activation path.

description: Experiment 3: improved browser restore continuity so dock-restored browser sessions no longer replay the fresh bottom-up sheet entry path. Added restoredFromDock marker to BrowserHostBrowserEntry, marked browser restores in BrowserHostState.restoreDockedSession, propagated restore semantics through AppRoot into AppBrowserSheetContainer, and added a restored browser activation path that snaps foreground state in place instead of animating from screen bottom. Restore continuity penalty dropped from 80 to 0 and targeted checks passed.

asi.hypothesis: The abrupt full-screen jump comes from treating restored browser sessions like fresh opens; marking restored browser entries and bypassing the bottom-up entry animation should make restore feel like resuming the same live surface.
asi.learned: A dedicated restored-from-dock semantic was missing only for browser entries; reader already had a restore semantic. Propagating that single bit through the host/container boundary is enough to stop the double-animation path.
asi.next_action_hint: Next experiments should move beyond static restore semantics into perceptual polish: maybe add a short settle/fade for restored browser content, or refine minimize/restore overlay geometry so browser and reader use even more live-surface continuity.

description: Baseline for browser restore settle polish. Current penalty is 90 because restored browser/reader sessions do not emit a fresh foregroundActivationKey on restore, and AppBrowserSheetContainer still lacks a dedicated in-place restore-settle helper/animation path.

asi.hypothesis: After removing the heavy fresh-open replay, the next perceptual gap is missing reactivation semantics and missing lightweight restore-settle motion.
asi.rollback_reason: Baseline only establishes the new target metric.
asi.next_action_hint: Increment foregroundActivationKey when restoring docked browser and reader sessions, then add a tiny in-place restore-settle helper and animation path in AppBrowserSheetContainer.
